# Sirach Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Children, listen to me — I am your father. Do what I say, and you will be safe.

**2** The Lord gave fathers authority over their children and established the rights of mothers over their sons.

**3** Honor your father, and your sins will be forgiven.

**4** Respect your mother, and you are building up a treasure.

**5** Honor your father, and your own children will bring you joy; your prayers will be answered.

**6** Respect your father, and you will live long. Obey the Lord, and your mother will find rest.

**7** Reverence for the Lord means honoring your father; it means treating your parents with the same respect you would show a master.

**8** Honor your father in what you say and what you do, so that his blessing will rest on you.

**9** A father's blessing builds a solid house for the children; a mother's curse tears out the very foundations.

**10** Don't try to get honor for yourself by dishonoring your father. That brings shame, not glory.

**11** Your own honor is bound up in your father's good reputation. A disgraced mother brings reproach on her children.

**12** My child, support your father in his old age. Don't cause him grief while he is still alive.

**13** Even if his mind begins to fail, be gentle with him. Don't treat him with contempt in any of his remaining days.

**14** The kindness you show your father will never be forgotten — it counts as an offering that covers your sins.

**15** When you are in trouble, it will come to your rescue. Like morning frost burned off by the sun, your sins will disappear.

**16** Abandoning your father is as bad as blasphemy. Treating your mother badly brings God's curse on you.

**17** My child, go about your work quietly and humbly, and you will be more beloved than any lavish giver.

**18** The higher you rise, the more you should bow down. Then you will find favor with the Lord.

**19** Many are exalted and celebrated in the world, but God shares his secrets with those who are humble.

**20** The Lord's power is immense — yet it is the humble who bring him glory.

**21** Don't chase after what is too hard for you. Don't try to investigate what lies beyond your reach.

**22** Think carefully about what you have been given. You have no need to pry into hidden things.

**23** Don't get drawn into matters that are not your business — what has already been shown to you is more than enough to understand.

**24** Overconfidence has led many people astray; faulty thinking has caused their judgment to collapse.

**25** Eyes cannot see without light; a person cannot be wise without knowledge.

**26** A stubborn heart will end in bitterness; a person who courts danger will be destroyed by it.

**27** A stubborn heart is weighed down by troubles; the sinner just keeps adding more sins to the pile.

**28** There is no cure for the proud person's wounds — because evil has put down deep roots in that person.

**29** A thoughtful person turns a proverb over in their mind; a wise person listens very carefully.

**30** Water puts out a blazing fire; giving to the needy puts out sin.

**31** Someone who does a good turn for others is thinking ahead — when they stumble, they will find a hand to hold.
